# VFD Pump Control Narrative: Template and P-1102 Example

## Design approach

- **Values stay in your spreadsheets.** The narrative refers to tags and alarm IDs by name and never copies ranges or setpoints. If a number appears in two documents, they will eventually disagree. The narrative describes *behaviour*. The I/O list and alarm database hold the *values*.
- **Values that aren't in either spreadsheet get one home.** Timers, debounces and fallback behaviour usually aren't in an I/O list or alarm database. The template gives them a dedicated table (Section 8) so they don't end up scattered through the prose.
- **Most of the text is identical for every pump.** Sections marked *[STANDARD]* describe the common pump module behaviour. Engineers fill in only the *[FILL]* sections. If a pump needs to differ from the standard, record it in Section 11 rather than editing the standard text.

Conventions:
- `<<…>>` = fill in.
- `[IO]` = value lives in the I/O list.
- `[ALM]` = value lives in the alarm database.

---

## Part 1: Template

```markdown
# Control Narrative — VFD Pump Module
## <<Tag>> — <<Service description>>

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Module tag | <<P-xxxx>> |
| Area / Unit | <<area>> / <<unit>> |
| P&ID | <<drawing no. / rev>> |
| I/O list ref | <<document no. / rev>> |
| Alarm DB ref | <<document no. / rev>> |
| Module type / library version | VFD_PUMP <<vX.Y>> |
| Author / Checked / Approved | <<>> / <<>> / <<>> |
| Revision | <<rev, date, description>> |

---

### 1. Purpose [FILL]
<<One or two sentences: what the pump moves, from where to where, and why.>>

### 2. Process context [FILL]
- Source: <<vessel/line>>
- Destination: <<vessel/line>>
- Upstream/downstream equipment that affects this pump: <<valves, other pumps>>
- Product / CIP service: <<product only | product + CIP | ...>>

### 3. Associated instruments and devices [FILL]
Tag names and function only. Ranges, units and setpoints: see [IO] and [ALM].

| Tag | Description | Role in this module |
|---|---|---|
| <<VFD tag>> | Variable frequency drive | Run/stop, speed ref, feedback, fault |
| <<>> | <<>> | <<permissive / interlock / monitor / indication>> |

Communication to VFD: <<hardwired | EtherNet/IP | PROFINET | ...>>

### 4. Modes and ownership [STANDARD]
| Mode | Commanded by | Speed reference source |
|---|---|---|
| Auto | Batch/sequence (owner = Program) | Batch system |
| Manual | Operator via HMI (owner = Operator) | Operator entry at HMI |
| Out of Service | Maintenance | None, pump cannot start |

- Mode changes Auto→Manual are bumpless. The pump keeps its current state and speed.
- Mode changes Manual→Auto: the pump takes the batch command at the next scan. <<or: is stopped first — state which>>.
- Interlocks act in ALL modes. Permissives apply to start commands in Auto and Manual.
- Local/remote: <<local control station present? Y/N. If Y, describe LOCAL behaviour.>>

### 5. Start permissives [FILL]
All must be TRUE for a start command to be accepted. If a permissive is false, the start is
refused and the reason is shown on the faceplate. A permissive that drops while running
does NOT stop the pump unless it is also listed as an interlock in Section 6.

| ID | Condition | Source tag | Bypassable (by whom) |
|---|---|---|---|
| PM-01 | VFD ready, no fault, comms healthy | <<VFD>> | No |
| PM-02 | No active interlock | — | No |
| PM-<<>> | <<>> | <<>> | <<>> |

### 6. Interlocks [FILL]
Interlocks stop the pump in all modes. Latched interlocks require (1) cause cleared,
(2) operator reset on faceplate, (3) new start command. The pump never auto-restarts
on interlock clear unless stated here.

| ID | Cause | Condition (setpoint ref) | Delay/debounce | Action | Latched? | Bypassable (by whom) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IL-01 | VFD fault | Fault bit from drive | — | Stop, alarm | Yes | No |
| IL-02 | Fail to start | No run feedback within T_FTS | T_FTS | Stop cmd, alarm | Yes | No |
| IL-03 | VFD comms loss | <<>> | T_COMM | <<>> | Yes | No |
| IL-<<>> | <<>> | <<[ALM] ID>> | <<>> | <<stop / ramp stop / coast>> | <<>> | <<>> |

Hardwired/safety functions (E-stop, STO, SIS) are outside this narrative.
Reference: <<SRS / electrical drawing>>. The PLC only monitors them.

### 7. Speed control [FILL where marked]
- Auto reference source: <<batch phase parameter / PID output / tag>>
- Manual reference: operator entry, limited to the same clamps as Auto
- Clamps: min/max speed per [IO] <<VFD speed ref tag>>
- Ramp up/down: set in VFD parameters <<param nos.>>; PLC does not ramp <<or: PLC ramps — state>>
- Minimum running speed rationale: <<cooling / seal / min flow>>
- Behaviour on loss of Auto reference (batch comms / bad quality): <<hold last | go to fallback speed | stop>>
- Stop method on normal stop: <<ramp | coast>>. On interlock stop: <<ramp | coast>>

### 8. Module parameters not held in I/O list or alarm DB [FILL]
| Parameter | Value | Units | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| T_FTS – fail-to-start delay | <<>> | s | <<>> |
| T_FTSP – fail-to-stop delay | <<>> | s | <<>> |
| T_COMM – comms loss delay | <<>> | s | <<>> |
| <<debounce / delay timers>> | <<>> | <<>> | <<>> |

### 9. Alarms [FILL]
Setpoints, priorities and deadbands live in [ALM]. Only the module response is listed here.

| Alarm DB ID | Description | Module response | Operator action |
|---|---|---|---|
| <<>> | <<>> | <<alarm only / interlock IL-xx>> | <<>> |

### 10. Batch / sequence interface [STANDARD + FILL]
Commands from batch: Start, Stop, Speed SP, Acquire/Release ownership.
Status to batch: Running, Stopped, Faulted, Interlocked, In Auto, Actual speed, Ready.
Batch response on module interlock: <<phase HOLD | phase ABORT | ...>>
Phase(s) using this module: <<>>

### 11. Deviations from standard module behaviour [FILL]
<<"None", or list each deviation with justification.>>

### 12. Power loss / restart [STANDARD]
On PLC or drive power restoration the pump stays stopped. Mode is retained.
The pump needs a new start command. Latched interlocks stay latched across power cycles
<<or: are cleared — state which>>.

### 13. HMI [STANDARD + FILL]
Standard VFD pump faceplate. Extra indications for this pump: <<e.g., PT trend, level switches>>

### 14. Open items / assumptions [FILL]
| # | Item | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|

### 15. Test checklist (FAT/SAT) [STANDARD + FILL]
- [ ] Start/stop Manual and Auto
- [ ] Each permissive blocks start
- [ ] Each interlock trips, latches, needs reset, no auto-restart
- [ ] Fail to start / fail to stop alarms
- [ ] Speed clamps enforced in both modes
- [ ] Loss of batch reference behaviour
- [ ] VFD comms loss behaviour
- [ ] Power-cycle behaviour
- [ ] <<pump-specific tests>>
```

---

## Part 2: Example for P-1102

The brief didn't specify some items. In those places I made a reasonable choice and marked it **⚠ ASSUMED**. Each one is also listed in Section 14 for your team to confirm.

```markdown
# Control Narrative — VFD Pump Module
## P-1102 — T-110 to T-120 Transfer Pump

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Module tag | P-1102 |
| Area / Unit | <<area>> / Mixing & Hold |
| P&ID | <<drawing no. / rev>> |
| I/O list ref | <<document no. / rev>> |
| Alarm DB ref | <<document no. / rev>> |
| Module type / library version | VFD_PUMP <<vX.Y>> |
| Revision | A — first issue |

### 1. Purpose
P-1102 transfers mixed product from mix tank T-110 to hold tank T-120. The batch system
sets the transfer rate.

### 2. Process context
- Source: T-110 (mix tank)
- Destination: T-120 (hold tank)
- Upstream/downstream equipment: <<T-110 outlet valve, T-120 inlet valve tags>> ⚠ ASSUMED
  present but not yet defined. Their state is not used in this narrative (see OI-3).
- Service: Product <<+ CIP? see OI-5>>

### 3. Associated instruments and devices
| Tag | Description | Role in this module |
|---|---|---|
| VFD-1102 ⚠ ASSUMED tag | P-1102 drive | Run/stop, speed ref, feedback, fault |
| LSL-110 | T-110 low level switch | Start permissive + dry-run interlock |
| LSH-120 | T-120 high level switch | Start permissive + overfill interlock |
| PT-1102 | P-1102 discharge pressure | High-pressure interlock, low-pressure alarm, indication |

Communication to VFD: <<fill>>

### 4. Modes and ownership
Standard. Normal operation is Auto under the batch system. Manual is used for
commissioning and recovery.

### 5. Start permissives
| ID | Condition | Source tag | Bypassable |
|---|---|---|---|
| PM-01 | VFD ready, no fault, comms healthy | VFD-1102 | No |
| PM-02 | No active interlock | — | No |
| PM-03 | T-110 not low (LSL-110 healthy/not low) | LSL-110 | No |
| PM-04 | T-120 not high (LSH-120 healthy/not high) | LSH-120 | No |
| PM-05 | PT-1102 signal good quality | PT-1102 | Maintenance only, Manual mode only ⚠ ASSUMED |

### 6. Interlocks
| ID | Cause | Condition | Delay | Action | Latched | Bypassable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IL-01 | VFD fault | Drive fault bit | — | Stop | Yes | No |
| IL-02 | Fail to start | No run feedback after start cmd | T_FTS | Remove run cmd, alarm | Yes | No |
| IL-03 | VFD comms loss | Comms status bad | T_COMM | Stop (drive set to stop on comms loss) | Yes | No |
| IL-04 | Dry run | LSL-110 = low | T_LSL | Stop, coast ⚠ ASSUMED | Yes | No |
| IL-05 | T-120 overfill | LSH-120 = high | T_LSH | Stop, ramp | Yes | No |
| IL-06 | High discharge pressure | PT-1102 ≥ HH, see [ALM] PT-1102 HH | T_PHH | Stop, ramp | Yes | No |
| IL-07 | Loss of prime / no flow | PT-1102 ≤ L, see [ALM], while running above min speed | T_PL | Stop ⚠ ASSUMED trip (alt: alarm only) | Yes | No |
| IL-08 | PT-1102 bad quality | Signal out of range / fault | T_BADPV | Stop in Auto; alarm only in Manual ⚠ ASSUMED | Yes | No |

Notes:
- LSL-110 and LSH-120 must be wired fail-safe, so that loss of signal reads as an alarm:
  LSL de-energises on low, LSH de-energises on high. ⚠ ASSUMED. Confirm against [IO] (OI-1).
- IL-04 to IL-06 protect equipment and product. They are not safety instrumented functions.
  If the HAZOP rates T-120 overfill as a safety or food-safety hazard, move it to the
  SRS (OI-2).
- E-stop acts through VFD STO, hardwired. The PLC monitors status only.

### 7. Speed control
- Auto reference: batch transfer phase speed setpoint for P-1102
- Manual reference: operator entry at HMI
- Clamps: min/max per [IO] VFD-1102 speed reference. The PLC also applies these to the
  batch setpoint.
- Ramps: VFD parameters <<param nos.>>. The PLC does not ramp.
- Loss of batch reference / bad quality: hold last good speed for T_COMM, then stop
  ⚠ ASSUMED (OI-4).
- Normal stop: ramp. Dry-run stop (IL-04): coast, so the pump stops sooner.

### 8. Module parameters (proposed, confirm at commissioning)
| Parameter | Value | Units | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| T_FTS – fail-to-start | 5 | s | Std library default |
| T_FTSP – fail-to-stop | 10 | s | Must exceed ramp-down time |
| T_COMM – comms loss | 2 | s | Std library default |
| T_LSL – LSL-110 debounce | 3 | s | Vortex/agitation splash at low level |
| T_LSH – LSH-120 debounce | 1 | s | Short. Overfill protection |
| T_PHH – high-pressure delay | 2 | s | Ride through valve-closing transients |
| T_PL – low-pressure delay | 15 | s | Allow line to fill on start |
| T_BADPV – bad PV delay | 2 | s | Std library default |

### 9. Alarms
| Alarm DB ID | Description | Module response | Operator action |
|---|---|---|---|
| <<ID>> | P-1102 VFD fault | IL-01 | Check drive display, reset |
| <<ID>> | P-1102 fail to start | IL-02 | Check MCC/disconnect/drive |
| <<ID>> | P-1102 comms fail | IL-03 | Check network |
| <<ID>> | T-110 low level (LSL-110) | IL-04 | Confirm tank empty/end of transfer |
| <<ID>> | T-120 high level (LSH-120) | IL-05 | Check T-120 inventory |
| <<ID>> | PT-1102 high-high | IL-06 | Check downstream valves / blockage |
| <<ID>> | PT-1102 high | Alarm only | Check downstream valve positions |
| <<ID>> | PT-1102 low (running) | IL-07 | Check suction, prime, T-110 outlet valve |
| <<ID>> | PT-1102 signal fault | IL-08 | Check transmitter |

### 10. Batch interface
- Phase(s) using this module: <<Transfer T-110→T-120>>
- On IL-01 to IL-03 or IL-06 to IL-08: phase goes to HOLD.
- On IL-04 (LSL-110) during transfer: <<end-of-transfer condition → phase COMPLETE, or HOLD?>>
  See OI-6. This needs a decision. Low level is often the *normal* end of a transfer.
- On IL-05 (LSH-120): phase HOLD.

### 11. Deviations from standard
- IL-04 uses coast stop instead of the standard ramp stop (dry-run protection).
- IL-08 behaves differently in Auto and Manual.

### 12. Power loss / restart
Standard.

### 13. HMI
Standard faceplate, plus: PT-1102 value and trend, LSL-110 and LSH-120 states,
T-110/T-120 levels if analog level is available.

### 14. Open items / assumptions
| # | Item | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-1 | Confirm LSL-110 / LSH-120 fail-safe wiring and contact sense in [IO] | <<>> | Open |
| OI-2 | Confirm with HAZOP that T-120 overfill and dry run are not SIFs | <<>> | Open |
| OI-3 | Should T-110 outlet / T-120 inlet valve positions be permissives? | <<>> | Open |
| OI-4 | Loss-of-batch-reference behaviour (hold vs stop) | <<>> | Open |
| OI-5 | Is P-1102 used during CIP? If so, add CIP mode & different setpoints | <<>> | Open |
| OI-6 | Is LSL-110 the normal end-of-transfer, or is the end set by T-110 analog level / totalised flow? | <<>> | Open |
| OI-7 | Confirm VFD tag and comms type | <<>> | Open |
| OI-8 | IL-07 low pressure: trip or alarm only | <<>> | Open |

### 15. Test checklist
Standard checklist, plus:
- [ ] Simulate LSL-110 low while running → coast stop, latched, phase response per OI-6
- [ ] Simulate LSH-120 high → ramp stop, phase HOLD
- [ ] Force PT-1102 to HH → trip after T_PHH
- [ ] Run against closed suction (water trial) → IL-07 after T_PL
- [ ] Disconnect PT-1102 → IL-08 behaviour in Auto and Manual
- [ ] Wire break on LSL-110 and LSH-120 → reads as alarm (fail-safe check)
```

---

## Suggestions for scaling to 120 modules

1. **Generate the header and Section 3 from the spreadsheets.** The tag lists, I/O and alarm references, and alarm IDs can be pulled automatically. This removes the most error-prone part of the hand-filling.
2. **Write the standard sections once, in a module type spec, and reference it.** Sections 4, 12, 13 and the base test checklist would live in a single "VFD_PUMP Standard Behaviour" document. Each pump narrative then only carries the differences.
3. **Watch Section 11.** If many pumps record the same deviation, it probably belongs in the library as a configurable option rather than in individual narratives.
4. **Section 14 often holds the most valuable content.** The P-1102 example has eight open items from a five-line brief. Getting those decided before code is written saves rework later in FAT.
